text:
alex_jensen: quick Q — we're finalizing the async job contract and I want to nail down cancel semantics + the polling schema. scenario: client POSTs job, polls /status, then calls /cancel while the job is finishing. how should status evolve so we don't flip-flop? :thinking:

maria_cho: short answer: terminal states must be monotonic. once a job is marked terminal (succeeded/failed/cancelled) it should never change. client cancel requests should be best-effort and expressed as "cancel_requested" metadata if the job already finished. :+1:

samir: sgtm. details matter tho — two common approaches we've seen:
1) Accept-cancel: /cancel returns 202 Accepted and the job moves to "cancelling" -> then to "cancelled" if stop succeeded. If the job completed before the cancel was processed, status stays "succeeded" and we include cancel_requested_at.
2) Logical-cancel: server records cancel request and marks job terminal "cancelled" immediately (even if work completed), but returns the work result in an audit field. this can surprise clients expecting the real output.

leah: I prefer #1. Avoids hiding the truth about whether work actually completed. Also helps with downstream metrics (we can count actual successes vs cancelled).

maria_cho: agree. also a few API-level recommendations for backcompat and client simplicity:
- canonical status enum: ["queued","running","cancelling","succeeded","failed","cancelled"]
- "terminal": boolean derived from status (true for succeeded/failed/cancelled) so old clients can still check a single flag
- include timestamps: created_at, started_at, completed_at, cancel_requested_at, cancelled_at (optional)
- include "result_present": boolean to indicate if result payload is available when terminal

alex_jensen: nice. what should /cancel return code be? 204 vs 202 vs 409 when already terminal?

samir: I think: if cancel request accepted -> 202 + body { "status": "cancelling", "cancel_requested_at": "..." }. if job already terminal -> 200 with the current status object (no-op). if request invalid -> 400/403 accordingly. 204 feels too opaque for clients that poll frequently.

leah: add a guard for race on spelling/breaking changes: older clients use "canceled" (one L). we should support both in status metadata or keep canonical but add a compatibility mapping in server responses. maybe expose an aliases array? e.g., "status_aliases": ["canceled"] if the canonical is "cancelled".

maria_cho: optional but useful. also recommend adding a small schema field so clients can validate easily: e.g. 

```json
{
  "job_id": "string",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "terminal": true,
  "created_at": "RFC3339",
  "started_at": "RFC3339|null",
  "completed_at": "RFC3339|null",
  "cancel_requested_at": "RFC3339|null",
  "cancelled_at": "RFC3339|null",
  "result_present": true,
  "result_url": "string|null",
  "status_aliases": ["canceled"]
}
```

alex_jensen: good. what about polling backoff / token TTL interplay? if clients poll with a short-lived poll token and then try to cancel after token expiry, should /cancel accept a separate auth or require the same token?

samir: separate auth for actions is more flexible. treat cancel as a normal authenticated POST/DELETE with its own scope. if the poll token expired, cancel should still work if the caller has cancel permission. For the polling endpoint, we should return a policy field: "accepts_cancels": true/false and "cancel_endpoint": "/jobs/{id}/cancel" so clients can discover.

leah: one more edge case: partial completion + idempotency. if a job emits side-effects (writes DB) and is then cancelled, we should surface a reconciliation hint: "effects_committed": true/false and "reconciliation_suggested": "run-compensating-action". not required for all jobs but good for customers to design around.

ci-bot: reminder: add an integration test that simulates this race (fast completion vs cancel) and asserts status monotonicity and presence of cancel_requested_at when appropriate.

alex_jensen: thanks all — action items:
- (maria) put canonical schema + examples in API spec PR.
- (samir) add /cancel behavior section + examples for 202 vs terminal no-op.
- (leah) add compatibility note for american/uk spelling and reconciliation hints.
- (ci-bot) CI test added for race sim.

maria_cho: I'll draft the PR today. ping me if you want to pair on examples.

samir: I'll add the tests and docs for headers (auth scope) + discovery fields.

leah: leaving a :+1: — this should cover the main surprises.

alex_jensen: awesome, thanks. we'll iterate in the PR.
